::: {#brief .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-sb-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The brief</p>
<dl class="lx-sb-facts">
<div><dt>The site</dt><dd><b>A Prairie Town home</b> or <b>the ridge wind farm</b>, behind one meter, through every hour of 2025.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Its hours</dt><dd>The hourly patterns of the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) grid in 2025, reshaped to EIA's monthly <span class="lx-term" data-term="capacity-factor">capacity factors</span>: modelled sites, not measured ones.</dd></div>
<div><dt>You decide</dt><dd>Home: solar (kW), a battery (kWh), a <span class="lx-term" data-term="heat-pump">heat pump</span>, the <span class="lx-term" data-term="tariff">tariff</span>. Farm: wind, a battery, an <span class="lx-term" data-term="electrolyzer">electrolyzer</span>, a hydrogen tank.</dd></div>
<div><dt>The engine works out</dt><dd>The cheapest way to run all 8,760 hours, a <span class="lx-term" data-term="linear-program">linear program</span>; then the bills, the CO₂ and the <span class="lx-term" data-term="net-present-value">NPV</span>.</dd></div>
<div><dt>It leaves out</dt><dd>Outages, taxes and incentives, storage from one week to the next, and costs that change over time.</dd></div>
</dl>
<p class="lx-hint">Open-ended: start from a preset, change one thing at a time, and copy the plan link to keep a plan.</p>
</div>
```
:::

## How the engine works, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="sb0-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- sb0-explain:start (written from data/sb0-site-bench.json and e0.json by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<dl class="lx-ideas"><dt>Decisions</dt><dd>Every hour: how much to buy and send back (home) or sell and spill (farm), what goes into and out of the battery, and what the electrolyzer and tank do.</dd><dt>Goal</dt><dd>The lowest yearly cost for the home, or the highest yearly revenue for the farm, with the sizes you set.</dd><dt>Rules</dt><dd>Each hour balances; nothing runs above its size; the battery loses 15% of what it stores; the line and the buyer's take are limits.</dd><dt>Time</dt><dd>All 8,760 hours of 2025, as 52 weeks and 31 December, one small <span class="lx-term" data-term="linear-program">linear program</span> each.</dd><dt>Tie rule</dt><dd>A tiny wear charge on battery use and, on the farm, a hair's preference for selling earlier in the week. Both are left out of every number shown.</dd><dt>Ties</dt><dd>Every total shown is the same on every least-cost schedule. With storage, the hour-by-hour schedule, and the hour counts read from it, can differ.</dd><dt>It holds when</dt><dd><ul><li>the weather and prices of 2025 are a fair guide to the next 25 or 30 years;</li><li>the sourced costs, converted to 2025 dollars, hold for the whole horizon;</li><li>the grid is always there to buy from (home) or to sell to, up to the line (farm).</li></ul></dd><dt>It leaves out</dt><dd><ul><li>storage carried from one week to the next (the check below measures what that changes);</li><li>outages, taxes, tax credits, incentives and financing;</li><li>how other plants respond to the site: the CO₂ uses one average factor (CF6 explains the difference).</li></ul></dd></dl><p class="lx-eyebrow">Checked on one full-year LP</p><p class="lx-hint">The test runs each preset again as one LP over all 8,760 hours, with storage free to carry across weeks.</p><table class="lx-facts"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Preset</th><th scope="col">NPV, 52 weeks and 31 ```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The linear program behind the bench</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- Each hour adds a balance row. For the home: bought − sent back + battery out − battery in = the home's use − solar.
- For the farm: sold + spilled + into the battery + into the electrolyzer − battery out = wind.
- The battery's [state of charge]{.lx-term term="state-of-charge"} is one more variable per hour: this hour's level = last hour's + 0.85 × charge − discharge.
- "Size it for me" makes the sizes decisions too, each charged its yearly cost through the [capital recovery factor]{.lx-term term="capital-recovery-factor"}. It runs on a few [representative weeks]{.lx-term term="representative-period"}, as [lesson 13](13-capstone.html) and [M3](m03-capacity-expansion.html) do.
- Storage and coupled carriers, modelling power, hydrogen and heat together ([M4](m04-storage-multienergy.html), in the Modeler tier), writes this model in Python.
